reasons: script.md line 'Eighty-seven percent said they'd pay a hundred or two hundred dollars a year for a service agreement': number, amounts, period and object all match the source sentence word for word ('Per the survey, 87% of homeowners are willing to pay either $100 or $200 annually for a service agreement'). Population is the homeowners asked (about 400), and the script keeps it to 'said they'd pay', a stated willingness, which is fair. No number mismatch.

script.md 'Will people pay for that?' points 'that' at OUR plan card (members first, a discount on every repair, one price billed monthly). The survey asked about a generic HVAC service agreement priced per year, not this plan. Answering our card's question with the 87% applies the finding to a product the source never tested. Overreach.

script.md 'And that money shows up every month, even in the slow weeks' follows the survey line directly, so it reads as if the surveyed $100 or $200 a year arrives monthly. The source says annually and says nothing about monthly billing or cash in slow weeks. Monthly billing is our plan design and must be said as ours (conditional), not as a result.

script.md 'The ACHR News asked homeowners': the source says the survey was conducted by Clear Seas Research with the publication. Attribution should name both, matching facts.json publisher and the planned card tag.

Fairness context: the same article reports 92% of responding contractors charge $200 or more and 48% charge $300 or more, above what 87% of homeowners said they would pay. The script's 'Will people pay?' yes-answer is not false but leans on the low end; the price on our card must not be implied as validated by the survey. Not a fail on its own; fixed by narrowing 'that' (fix 1).

brief.md 'Do this week' send card text (THE MEMBER PLAN / TWO TUNE-UPS A YEAR / MEMBERS FIRST WHEN IT BREAKS / A DISCOUNT ON EVERY REPAIR / ONE PRICE, BILLED MONTHLY) carries no EXAMPLE or 'our suggested plan' label in its planned strings, though the claims table and facts.json say it is labeled EXAMPLE. As written, the card could read as an industry standard. Label must be in the card itself.

Story elements: 'Picture the first cold night', forty calls, three trucks are framed as a picture and marked EXAMPLE in the brief Shape; fine as long as the EXAMPLE chip is on screen during that beat. 'Members go first. They pay every month, so they jump the line' is plan logic, not a claim about real shops; acceptable as the rule of your own plan, and the script never claims plans raise income or that shops grow. Good.

Source age: Dec 2023, nearly three years old at posting. The planned card tag already reads 'Dec 2023; survey with Clear Seas Research'; that must stay on screen, and saying '2023' in the voice is the cleaner fix since the script is the only place most viewers hear the source.

Trades first: HVAC trade press (ACHR News) with a research firm, homeowner population; passes. The lesson's audience includes plumbing shops but the survey is HVAC agreements; the script's no-heat framing keeps it HVAC, so no caveat needed.
No em or en dashes found in script.md, brief.md or facts.json. No real private person or business named.
fixes: script.md: replace 'Will people pay for that? The ACHR News asked homeowners. Eighty-seven percent said they'd pay a hundred or two hundred dollars a year for a service agreement.' with 'Will people pay for a plan? In a 2023 survey, The ACHR News and Clear Seas Research asked about four hundred homeowners. Eighty-seven percent said they'd pay a hundred or two hundred dollars a year for a service agreement.'

script.md: replace 'And that money shows up every month, even in the slow weeks when the phone barely rings.' with 'Bill it monthly, and that money comes in even in the slow weeks when the phone barely rings.'
brief.md send card: add a visible label line 'EXAMPLE: OUR SUGGESTED PLAN' to the card strings (Do this week and Send), so the plan card never reads as a standard or a survey result.
brief.md Real screens: keep the tag 'The ACHR News, with Clear Seas Research, Dec 2023, about 400 homeowners' on the 87% card for the whole beat.

Optional, sourced support for the card (same page): homeowners expect at least two service visits a year; 80% want parts discounts, 78% labor discounts, 77% priority service. Use only if quoted as the survey with the same tag; do not merge into the EXAMPLE card.
